meta.title: PVA:ALG Hybrid Bioink for Biofabrication of 3D Neural Models.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A PVA/alginate hybrid ink was optimized for printability and used to build scaffolds for SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. The hybrid supported viability and ECM formation for 15 days, better than 2D culture.

formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 4.6 psi. Cells were seeded onto printed scaffolds, not printed inside the ink.
formulations.name: PVA:ALG hybrid (16% PVA / 15% ALG)
formulations.composition_detail: 16 wt% PVA and 15 wt% alginate, 1:1 v/v
formulations.key_outcome: Hybrid scaffolds kept SH-SY5Y cells viable for 15 days, outperforming 2D culture.

evidence.quote: Further characterizations were carried out using 16% PVA and 15% ALG, while a 25G nozzle and 4.6 psi pressure were utilized for bioprinting.
25G nozzle diameter, 10 mm/s printing speed, and 50% infill density
the Young’s modulus increased from 1.6 kPa (N-XD) to 2.34 kPa (XD)
Neural cell proliferation, viability, and morphology were analyzed by culturing SH-SY5Y human neuroblastoma cells in 3D on hybrid scaffolds.
